title: Computation-based autism prediction from behavioral data: a systematic review of study design, conduct and reporting
objective: To characterise how computation-based (machine learning and other computational) autism prediction studies that use behavioral data are designed, conducted and reported: who is studied and how they are described, in what settings and with what tasks, hardware and software the behavioral data are collected, how datasets are shared and how reproducibility and bias are handled, which behavioral modalities are operationalised and how they are combined, which computational methods, representations, evaluation metrics, interpretability techniques and validation strategies are used, and how the publication landscape has evolved over time.
pico_population: Human participants assessed in relation to autism spectrum disorder (autistic/ASD participants and any comparison groups, including neurotypical participants and participants with other diagnoses), at any age, from infancy to adulthood.
pico_intervention: Computational methods (machine learning, deep learning, statistical classifiers or other computational models) applied to behavioral data - gaze/eye movement, facial expression and affect, speech, voice, prosody and language, gestures, motor behavior and kinematics, posture and gait, touch/interaction traces, activity and social-interaction patterns - to predict, screen for, classify, or estimate the severity of autism.
pico_comparison: A clinical or reference-standard autism determination (e.g. DSM-5/ICD criteria, ADOS/ADOS-2, ADI-R, clinician diagnosis) or an established screening instrument, and/or a non-autistic or other-diagnosis comparison group.
pico_outcome: Reported study, participant, data and model characteristics: study goals and main findings; setting, data provenance and collection protocol; temporal design and privacy handling; acquisition hardware and software; dataset access conditions and reproducibility provisions; dataset bias, imbalance and acknowledged limitations; stated future directions; behavioral modalities used and how they are fused; computational approaches, input representations, evaluation metrics, interpretability methods and informative features; robustness, generalizability, bias mitigation and validation strategy; and publication-venue and temporal trends.
inclusion_criteria: Peer-reviewed journal articles, conference papers or workshop papers that (1) apply a computational or machine-learning model to (2) behavioral data collected from or about human participants, in order to (3) predict, screen for, classify, or estimate the severity of autism spectrum disorder, and (4) report enough methodological detail (participants, data, model, evaluation) to be charted. Any age group, any country, any behavioral modality, any study setting (laboratory, clinic, home, school, remote/online), primary data collection or secondary analysis of existing datasets, published in any year.
exclusion_criteria: Reports that are not primary computational studies (narrative reviews, systematic reviews, meta-analyses, editorials, commentaries, protocols, abstract-only conference records); studies whose predictive input is not behavioral (e.g. genetic, neuroimaging-only, blood-biomarker-only, or electronic health record data with no behavioral observation); studies that model autism-related constructs without any autism prediction, screening, classification or severity-estimation target; studies of intervention effectiveness or therapy outcome without a prediction task; reports whose full text could not be read; and duplicate records of an already-included report.
databases: Not yet declared by the reviewer - user-supplied corpus
charting_questions: RQ1.1 Which participant groups are included (autistic/ASD, neurotypical, other diagnoses), and is each group's presence and size explicitly reported?
RQ1.2 What terminology does the paper use for its participant groups (e.g. 'autistic person', 'person with autism', 'ASD group', 'control', 'typically developing')? Quote the terms used.
RQ1.3 What are the sample size, age range and mean/SD, and gender distribution per group, and are comparison groups explicitly matched to autistic participants on age and/or gender?
RQ1.4 How is autism diagnosed or confirmed (which standardized instruments, e.g. ADOS/ADOS-2, ADI-R, DSM-5/ICD, clinician diagnosis, parent report, or dataset label only)?
RQ1.5 Are additional cognitive, linguistic or adaptive-functioning measures reported (e.g. IQ, VABS, language level), and are comorbid conditions described or used as exclusions?

RQ2.1 What is the primary goal of the study (screening vs diagnosis, binary classification vs multi-class vs severity estimation vs prediction of a clinical outcome), and what are the main findings the authors report against that goal?
RQ2.2 In which setting were the data collected (laboratory, clinic, home, school, remote/online, unspecified), and does the study use an existing dataset, newly collected data, or a combination?

RQ2.3 What tasks, activities or protocols were used during data collection (e.g. free viewing, joint-attention probe, ADOS administration, gameplay, imitation task, conversation, robot interaction), or was data collection task-free/naturalistic?

RQ2.4 Are the data cross-sectional or longitudinal, over what time scale (session duration, number of sessions, follow-up), and do they contain sensitive information (video, audio, faces, identifiable speech)? If so, how are privacy, anonymization, consent and data protection addressed?
RQ2.5 Which hardware and software were used to acquire the behavioral data (eye tracker model, camera, microphone, Kinect/IMU, tablet, robot platform, acquisition software)?

RQ2.6 What are the access conditions for the dataset (open, restricted, proprietary, available on request, not stated), and how is reproducibility addressed (code availability, model/hyperparameter reporting, random seeds, preprocessing detail, public benchmark)?

RQ2.7 What sources of dataset bias or imbalance are reported or identifiable (class imbalance, age, sex/gender skew, ethnicity, single-site recruitment, IQ range), and what limitations are acknowledged by the authors or identified during this review regarding design, data or methods?
RQ2.9 What future research directions or open questions do the authors propose?

RQ3.1 Which types of behavioral data are used (gaze/eye movement, facial expression, speech, voice/prosody, language content, gesture, motor/kinematics, posture/gait, touch/interaction logs, activity patterns, questionnaire-recorded behavior)?

RQ3.2 If more than one behavioral modality is used, how are they combined (feature concatenation, early/intermediate/late fusion, decision-level voting, separate per-modality models compared), and are behavioral data combined with non-behavioral data (clinical scores, demographics, parent report)?

RQ4.1 Which machine-learning paradigm is used (supervised, unsupervised, self-supervised, reinforcement, none/statistical), and which specific algorithms (linear models, SVM/kernel methods, tree ensembles, CNN, RNN/LSTM, transformer, graph networks, other)?
RQ4.2 How are behaviors represented as model inputs (raw time series, handcrafted/statistical features, images or scanpath renderings, deep embeddings, symbolic/event-based representations, text)?
RQ4.3 Which evaluation metrics are reported (accuracy, sensitivity/recall, specificity, precision, F1, AUC/ROC, PR-AUC, kappa, MAE/RMSE for severity), and what are the headline values?

RQ4.4 Which interpretability or explanation methods are used (feature importance, SHAP, LIME, saliency/Grad-CAM, attention weights, coefficient inspection, ablation), and which behavioral features emerge as most informative?

RQ4.5 How are robustness, generalizability, bias and deployment readiness evaluated - cross-validation scheme (and whether it is nested or subject-independent), external/independent test set, held-out site, class-imbalance handling or bias mitigation, statistical comparison, and any real-time or near-real-time/deployment claim?
RQ5.1 Which keywords and terms does the paper use to describe this line of work (author keywords, index terms, and the vocabulary used for the prediction task)?
RQ5.2 In which venue was it published (journal, conference or workshop; name), and is that venue primarily autism/clinical-focused, broader biomedical, or technology/computational?
RQ5.3 What is the publication year, and does the paper itself characterise the field's growth, shifting modalities, methods or age ranges over time?
default_group_questions: What are the typical participant groups, sample sizes and age ranges in this modality group, and how is autism confirmed?
Which data-collection settings, tasks and acquisition hardware dominate this modality?
Which computational approaches, input representations and validation strategies are most common here, and what performance is reported?
How are datasets shared and reproducibility addressed in this modality group?
Which sources of bias, imbalance or limitation recur in this modality, and what future directions do these authors propose?
appraisal_domains: Behavioral Data Collection, Predictors and Reference Standard (PROBAST: predictors, outcome)
